title: From Nobody To History: The Story Of Franklin Pierce #Shorts
description:
The rise of Franklin Pierce was not an accident — in retrospect the pattern is plain. Franklin Pierce (November 23, 1804 – October 8, 1869) was the 14th president of the United States, serving from 1853 to 1857. A northern Democrat who believed that the abolitionist movement was a fundamental threat to national unity, he alienated anti-slavery groups by signing the Kansas–Nebraska Act and enforcing the Fugitive Slave Act.

Money, luck and timing all played their parts in the life of Franklin Pierce — in that order. Pierce's term began in March 1833, but he would not be sworn in until Congress met in December, and his attention was elsewhere. Franklin and Benjamin Pierce were among the prominent citizens who welcomed President Jackson to the state on his visit in mid-1833.
